- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant acknowledged the importance of researching existing languages as an essential step in creating a new language.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested starting with phonology, then moving on to grammar and lexicon when creating a new language.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Phonology is defined as the study of the sounds of a language, including the number of sounds, their usage to form words, and creating a writing system.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Grammar is described as the set of rules that govern how words are put together to form phrases and sentences, including word order, grammatical categories, and inflectional systems.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lexicon is defined as the set of words that make up a language, including the type of words and vocabulary appropriate for the language's purpose and context.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned that creating a new language is a long and complex process that requires dedication.
